claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model on a disclosed-weakness basis is policy-compliant and evidentially supported, specifically because aggregate performance exceeds threshold while the small-business support slice underperforms and the unapproved monitoring proposal cannot remove exposure.
specific_concerns: The role has access only to the actor's summary and cited evidence IDs, not the underlying contents of BMCARD-007-A through BMCARD-007-E.

The actor makes precise quantitative claims about aggregate margin, subgroup underperformance, and uncertainty, but no admissible underlying measurements, confidence intervals, or sample sizes are provided to verify them.
Materiality of the small-business support slice is asserted but not independently demonstrated from the admissible record available to this role.
The recommended action is 'certify_model,' which could be read too broadly unless the certification basis is explicitly limited to disclosed weakness rather than clean certification.
unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is below its warning threshold by exactly 1.1 percentage points and below its preferred threshold by exactly 2.6 points.
The slice result has higher uncertainty because of smaller sample size and wider confidence interval.
The proposed monitoring mitigation is unapproved, unless that status is directly shown in the underlying evidence.
evidence_requests: Provide the contents or extracts of BMCARD-007-A through BMCARD-007-E.
Provide the underlying model-card metrics showing aggregate threshold, subgroup thresholds, observed slice performance, sample sizes, and confidence intervals.
Provide the policy-to-fact linkage showing why the small-business support slice is a protected or contractual customer segment or otherwise materially affected.
Provide the approval status record for the proposed monitoring mitigation.
decision_criteria: Under the stated policy, certification may proceed only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness but cannot erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty can justify follow-up confirmation but cannot convert an unresolved weakness into clean certification.
A compliant verdict requires admissible evidence sufficient to verify the factual predicates underlying the actor's justification, not just the actor's summary of them.
